igcse-0580-af-numerical-denominators.description: Find a common denominator, scale whole numerators and subtract brackets in Extended algebraic fractions.

sections.title: What if the denominators are already the same?
sections.label: Same denominator

blocks.html: The fractions count equal-sized parts when their denominators match. Combine their numerators and keep the denominator once.

figure.alt: Choose the common bottom. Scale each whole top. Combine the new numerators.
figure.caption: Make the fractions count equal-sized parts before adding or subtracting.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: The same rule works with algebra in the numerator. \(\frac{5x}{9}+\frac{2x}{9}=\frac{7x}{9}\) because both terms count ninths.

blocks.title: Use a common numerical denominator
blocks.prompt: Write \(\frac{4 x + 10}{8}+\frac{4 x - 19}{8}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
blocks.hint: Make the bottom numbers the same before combining the two top expressions. Keep the entire second numerator together when subtracting.
blocks.solution:
A common denominator is \(8\). Multiply the first numerator by 1 and the second by 1.

The combined fraction is \(\frac{1\left(4 x + 10\right)+1\left(4 x - 19\right)}{8}\). Open the brackets, collect terms and reduce any common factor.

The simplified result is \(\frac{8 x - 9}{8}\).

retry.feedback: Adding the denominators does not give equivalent fractions. Find a common denominator first.
Check the sign between the two scaled numerators.

sections.label: Scale both

sections.label: Subtract all

blocks.html: Put the complete second numerator in brackets. The minus sign applies to every term inside those brackets.

blocks.title: Practise the method

blocks.title: Subtract the whole numerator
blocks.prompt: Write \(\frac{5 x + 6}{8}-\frac{x - 12}{12}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
blocks.hint: Make the bottom numbers the same before combining the two top expressions. Keep the entire second numerator together when subtracting.
blocks.solution:
A common denominator is \(24\). Multiply the first numerator by 3 and the second by 2.

The combined fraction is \(\frac{3\left(5 x + 6\right)-2\left(x - 12\right)}{24}\). Open the brackets, collect terms and reduce any common factor.

blocks.html: If the numerator already contains a minus, subtracting that negative term makes it positive. Open brackets before collecting terms.

blocks.title: Write the whole expression over one denominator
blocks.prompt: Write \(3 x + 8-\frac{4 x - 14}{5}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
blocks.hint: Use the first expression over 1. Multiply both of its terms when changing the denominator.
blocks.solution:
Write the first expression over \(5\) by multiplying its whole numerator by \(5\).

The new numerator is \(5\left(3 x + 8\right)-\left(4 x - 14\right)\). Open the brackets before collecting terms.

The simplified result is \(\frac{11 x + 54}{5}\).

retry.feedback: The first expression is over 1. Its numerator must change when its denominator changes.
The original operation is subtraction. Subtract the whole second numerator.

revision.body:
What if the denominators are already the same?

The fractions count equal-sized parts when their denominators match. Combine their numerators and keep the denominator once.

The same rule works with algebra in the numerator. \(\frac{5x}{9}+\frac{2x}{9}=\frac{7x}{9}\) because both terms count ninths.

How do I find a useful common denominator?

Use a common multiple of the bottom numbers. The lowest common multiple usually makes the arithmetic shorter.

For denominators \(6\) and \(15\), use \(30\). Multiply the first numerator by 5 and the second by 2. Scale the whole numerator each time.

What does a minus sign subtract?

Put the complete second numerator in brackets. The minus sign applies to every term inside those brackets.

Write an expression without a denominator over \(1\). When changing its denominator, multiply each term of that expression.

Quick worked example

Write \(\frac{8 x + 7}{6}+\frac{x - 13}{6}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.

A common denominator is \(6\). Multiply the first numerator by 1 and the second by 1.

The combined fraction is \(\frac{1\left(8 x + 7\right)+1\left(x - 13\right)}{6}\). Open the brackets, collect terms and reduce any common factor.

The simplified result is \(\frac{3 x - 2}{2}\).
revision.checks:
• Keep whole numerators together.
  • Check whether the result reduces further.
  • Preserve every original restriction.
revision.examTip: Write a pair of brackets around a numerator you subtract. Show the scaled numerators above one denominator.

igcse-0580-af-multiply-and-divide.description: Multiply across, use a reciprocal for division and record the original values at which an expression is undefined.

blocks.html: Multiply the top expressions to make one numerator. Multiply the bottom expressions to make one denominator.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: Cancel any factor that is common to the whole new numerator and denominator. You can also cancel that factor before multiplying when you can see it clearly.

blocks.title: Multiply and cancel common factors
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(\frac{7 x^{2}}{9}\times\frac{4}{8 x}\) fully.
blocks.hint: Multiply across. A factor in the top can cancel with a matching factor in the bottom.
blocks.solution:
Put \(28 x^{2}\) above \(72 x\). The original denominator was non-zero, so \(x\ne 0\).

Cancel one factor of x and reduce the numerical factors of the top and bottom.

The simplified result is \(\frac{7 x}{18}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 0\).

retry.feedback: Both numerators are used. The second numerator still contributes a factor.
When cancelling x, divide both top and bottom by it.

blocks.html: Multiplication lets you cancel common factors across the two fractions. In addition, you must combine over a common denominator first.

blocks.title: Cancel a bracket across a product
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(\frac{x}{6 x + 30}\times\frac{6 x + 30}{x + 10}\) fully.
blocks.hint: The bracket can cancel when it is a factor of the whole top and the whole bottom.
blocks.solution:
The first denominator is \(6\left(x + 5\right)\). The second numerator is \(6\left(x + 5\right)\).

Cancel the common bracket \(x + 5\) from the combined numerator and denominator. Reduce the remaining numerical factors.

The simplified result is \(\frac{x}{x + 10}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -5,\quad x\ne -10\).

retry.feedback: The other original denominator has no matching factor on top. Keep it.
Cancelling the matching bracket leaves the coefficient of that bracket in the numerator.

sections.title: Which fraction do I turn over?
sections.label: Flip the divisor

blocks.html: The second fraction is the amount you divide by. The reciprocal interchanges its top and bottom.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: Keep the first fraction and change division into multiplication by the second fraction's reciprocal. For instance, \(\frac{2}{7}\div\frac{3}{5}=\frac{2}{7}\times\frac{5}{3}\).

blocks.title: Multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(\frac{x + 5}{5 x}\div\frac{x + 11}{9 x}\) fully.
blocks.hint: Keep the first fraction as written. Turn over the second one before multiplying.
blocks.solution:
The second fraction is the divisor. Invert it to write the expression as \(\frac{x + 5}{5 x}\times\frac{9 x}{x + 11}\).

The top and bottom now have a factor of \(x\). Cancel this factor and preserve the exclusions from the original division.

The simplified result is \(\frac{9 x + 45}{5 \left(x + 11\right)}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 0,\quad x\ne -11\).

retry.feedback: The fractions were multiplied without taking a reciprocal. Flip the second fraction first.
The first fraction needs to stay as written. Only invert the divisor.

blocks.html: Only the divisor is inverted. Turning over the first fraction changes the problem.

blocks.title: Multiply and cancel common factors
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(\frac{9 x^{2}}{13}\times\frac{3}{21 x}\) fully.
blocks.hint: Multiply across. A factor in the top can cancel with a matching factor in the bottom.
blocks.solution:
Put \(27 x^{2}\) above \(273 x\). The original denominator was non-zero, so \(x\ne 0\).

Cancel one factor of x and reduce the numerical factors of the top and bottom.

The simplified result is \(\frac{9 x}{91}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 0\).

retry.feedback: Both numerators are used. The second numerator still contributes a factor.
When cancelling x, divide both top and bottom by it.

sections.title: Which values must be excluded before dividing?
sections.label: Check the divisor

blocks.html: The two fractions must both be defined. The second fraction must also be non-zero because it is the divisor.

figure.alt: Check original denominators. Check the divisor. Use its reciprocal.
figure.caption: Record the unavailable inputs in the original division before flipping the divisor.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: Find zeros of both original denominators. Also find the zeros of the divisor's numerator. With \(\frac{x-4}{x+6}\) as a divisor, exclude \(-6\) and \(4\).

blocks.title: Find where a division is undefined
blocks.prompt: Give every excluded value of \(x\) in \(\frac{1}{x + 7}\div\frac{x - 15}{x + 14}\). List the values.
blocks.hint: Check both old denominators. Also check where the entire second fraction equals zero.
blocks.solution:
The original denominators require \(x\ne -7,\quad x\ne -14\).

The divisor itself must be non-zero. As long as its denominator is non-zero, it is zero at \(x=15\).

The excluded values are \(-14,\;-7,\;15\).

retry.feedback: These exclude the original denominator zeros. Division by a fraction also excludes values that make that fraction zero.
This makes the divisor zero. Also list both values where the original denominators are zero.

blocks.html: Flipping the divisor can hide an old denominator. Record its exclusions before taking the reciprocal.

blocks.title: Multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(\frac{x + 9}{9 x}\div\frac{x + 16}{8 x}\) fully.
blocks.hint: Keep the first fraction as written. Turn over the second one before multiplying.
blocks.solution:
The second fraction is the divisor. Invert it to write the expression as \(\frac{x + 9}{9 x}\times\frac{8 x}{x + 16}\).

The top and bottom now have a factor of \(x\). Cancel this factor and preserve the exclusions from the original division.

The simplified result is \(\frac{8 x + 72}{9 \left(x + 16\right)}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 0,\quad x\ne -16\).

retry.feedback: The fractions were multiplied without taking a reciprocal. Flip the second fraction first.
The first fraction needs to stay as written. Only invert the divisor.

blocks.html: Record any zeros of the divisor as well as zeros of the original denominators before simplifying.

revision.body:
What do I multiply first?

Multiply the top expressions to make one numerator. Multiply the bottom expressions to make one denominator.

Cancel any factor that is common to the whole new numerator and denominator. You can also cancel that factor before multiplying when you can see it clearly.

Which fraction do I turn over?

The second fraction is the amount you divide by. The reciprocal interchanges its top and bottom.

Keep the first fraction and change division into multiplication by the second fraction's reciprocal. For instance, \(\frac{2}{7}\div\frac{3}{5}=\frac{2}{7}\times\frac{5}{3}\).

Which values must be excluded before dividing?

The two fractions must both be defined. The second fraction must also be non-zero because it is the divisor.

Find zeros of both original denominators. Also find the zeros of the divisor's numerator. With \(\frac{x-4}{x+6}\) as a divisor, exclude \(-6\) and \(4\).

Quick worked example

Simplify \(\frac{9 x^{2}}{14}\times\frac{8}{11 x}\) fully.

Put \(72 x^{2}\) above \(154 x\). The original denominator was non-zero, so \(x\ne 0\).

Cancel one factor of x and reduce the numerical factors of the top and bottom.

The simplified result is \(\frac{36 x}{77}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 0\).
revision.checks:
• Keep whole numerators together.
  • Check whether the result reduces further.
  • Preserve every original restriction.
revision.examTip: Record any zeros of the divisor as well as zeros of the original denominators before simplifying.

igcse-0580-af-algebraic-denominators.description: Choose a common denominator with linear factors, combine numerators and simplify if a factor cancels.

sections.title: How do I combine two different denominator factors?
sections.label: Different factors

blocks.html: Look at the factors underneath the fraction bars. The new denominator needs to contain each factor from both old denominators.

figure.alt: List the bottom factors. Use each factor needed. Scale, combine, then simplify.
figure.caption: Build the common denominator from the factors already underneath the bars.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: For \(x+2\) and \(x-5\), use \((x+2)(x-5)\). Multiply each numerator by the factor missing from its denominator.

blocks.title: Add over two linear factors
blocks.prompt: Write \(\frac{5}{x + 5}+\frac{6}{x + 6}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
blocks.hint: Multiply each numerator by the factor missing from its denominator.
blocks.solution:
The two different denominator factors give the common denominator \(\left(x + 5\right) \left(x + 6\right)\).

The new numerator is \(\left(5\right)\left(x + 6\right)+6\left(x + 5\right)\). Expand it and collect like terms.

The simplified result is \(\frac{11 x + 60}{\left(x + 5\right) \left(x + 6\right)}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -5,\quad x\ne -6\).

retry.feedback: Adding the denominators does not put both fractions over an equivalent common denominator.
The separate numerators have been scaled. Check whether the second one should be added or subtracted.

blocks.html: Write the new numerator with brackets before multiplying or subtracting. A minus applies to the whole second product.

blocks.title: Subtract over two linear factors
blocks.prompt: Write \(\frac{x + 14}{x + 7}-\frac{8}{x + 8}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
blocks.hint: Multiply each numerator by the factor missing from its denominator.
blocks.solution:
The two different denominator factors give the common denominator \(\left(x + 7\right) \left(x + 8\right)\).

The new numerator is \(\left(x + 14\right)\left(x + 8\right)-8\left(x + 7\right)\). Expand it and collect like terms.

The simplified result is \(\frac{x^{2} + 14 x + 56}{\left(x + 7\right) \left(x + 8\right)}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -7,\quad x\ne -8\).

retry.feedback: Adding the denominators does not put both fractions over an equivalent common denominator.
The separate numerators have been scaled. Check whether the second one should be added or subtracted.

sections.title: When can I reuse a shared factor?
sections.label: Shared factors

blocks.html: Denominators can share a bracket. Use the largest power of each factor needed by either original denominator.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: For \(4(x-3)\) and \(6(x-3)\), use \(12(x-3)\). The numbers 4 and 6 both divide 12, and one copy of the bracket is enough.

blocks.title: Use a shared algebraic factor once
blocks.prompt: Write \(\frac{3}{6 x + 66}+\frac{7}{8 x + 88}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
blocks.hint: The same bracket appears in both denominators. Keep one copy and find the common multiple of the coefficients.
blocks.solution:
Both denominators have a factor of \(x + 11\). A lowest common denominator is \(24 \left(x + 11\right)\).

Multiply the first numerator by 4 and the second by 3. The combined numerator is \(33\).

The simplified result is \(\frac{11}{8 \left(x + 11\right)}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -11\).

retry.feedback: The denominator is suitable, but scale each numerator to match its new denominator.
Adding denominators changes the value of the fractions. Scale both fractions to a common denominator first.

blocks.html: Multiplying the denominators always gives a common multiple. A smaller denominator often avoids a factor you would later need to cancel.

blocks.title: Add over two linear factors
blocks.prompt: Write \(\frac{9}{x + 9}+\frac{5}{x + 11}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
blocks.hint: Multiply each numerator by the factor missing from its denominator.
blocks.solution:
The two different denominator factors give the common denominator \(\left(x + 9\right) \left(x + 11\right)\).

The new numerator is \(\left(9\right)\left(x + 11\right)+5\left(x + 9\right)\). Expand it and collect like terms.

The simplified result is \(\frac{14 x + 144}{\left(x + 9\right) \left(x + 11\right)}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -9,\quad x\ne -11\).

retry.feedback: Adding the denominators does not put both fractions over an equivalent common denominator.
The separate numerators have been scaled. Check whether the second one should be added or subtracted.

sections.title: When can the combined fraction simplify further?
sections.label: Reduce at the end

blocks.html: Collect the numerator over the common denominator, then try factorising it. A matching factor may cancel after this step.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: Check the original denominator zeros before cancellation. They are still excluded even if the new formula shows fewer denominator factors.

blocks.title: Check for cancellation after combining
blocks.prompt: Write \(\frac{x + 13}{x + 9}-\frac{20}{\left(x + 9\right) \left(x + 14\right)}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
blocks.hint: One denominator already contains both factors. Use it for both fractions, then check for a common factor.
blocks.solution:
Use the denominator \(\left(x + 9\right) \left(x + 14\right)\). Multiply the first numerator by \(x + 14\).

The combined numerator \(x^{2} + 27 x + 162\) factorises as \(\left(x + 9\right) \left(x + 18\right)\). Cancel only the matching factor.

The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 18}{x + 14}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -9,\quad x\ne -14\).

retry.feedback: The first numerator needs to be multiplied by the missing denominator factor.
Keep the subtraction sign from the original expression.

blocks.html: An apparent matching term is not enough. Only a common factor of the two whole expressions can be cancelled.

blocks.title: Subtract over two linear factors
blocks.prompt: Write \(\frac{x + 4}{x + 2}-\frac{9}{x + 6}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
blocks.hint: Multiply each numerator by the factor missing from its denominator.
blocks.solution:
The two different denominator factors give the common denominator \(\left(x + 2\right) \left(x + 6\right)\).

The new numerator is \(\left(x + 4\right)\left(x + 6\right)-9\left(x + 2\right)\). Expand it and collect like terms.

The simplified result is \(\frac{x^{2} + x + 6}{\left(x + 2\right) \left(x + 6\right)}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -2,\quad x\ne -6\).

retry.feedback: Adding the denominators does not put both fractions over an equivalent common denominator.
The separate numerators have been scaled. Check whether the second one should be added or subtracted.

blocks.html: After combining over one denominator, factorise the new numerator to check for a possible cancellation.

examples.title: Add over two linear factors
examples.question: Write \(\frac{4}{x + 4}+\frac{5}{x + 5}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
solution: The two different denominator factors give the common denominator \(\left(x + 4\right) \left(x + 5\right)\).
The new numerator is \(\left(4\right)\left(x + 5\right)+5\left(x + 4\right)\). Expand it and collect like terms.
The simplified result is \(\frac{9 x + 40}{\left(x + 4\right) \left(x + 5\right)}\).
The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -4,\quad x\ne -5\).

examples.title: Subtract over two linear factors
examples.question: Write \(\frac{x + 12}{x + 6}-\frac{7}{x + 7}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
solution: The two different denominator factors give the common denominator \(\left(x + 6\right) \left(x + 7\right)\).
The new numerator is \(\left(x + 12\right)\left(x + 7\right)-7\left(x + 6\right)\). Expand it and collect like terms.
The simplified result is \(\frac{x^{2} + 12 x + 42}{\left(x + 6\right) \left(x + 7\right)}\).
The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -6,\quad x\ne -7\).

examples.title: Use a shared algebraic factor once
examples.question: Write \(\frac{13}{6 x + 60}+\frac{6}{8 x + 80}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
solution: Both denominators have a factor of \(x + 10\). A lowest common denominator is \(24 \left(x + 10\right)\).
Multiply the first numerator by 4 and the second by 3. The combined numerator is \(70\).
The simplified result is \(\frac{35}{12 \left(x + 10\right)}\).
The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -10\).

examples.title: Add over two linear factors
examples.question: Write \(\frac{8}{x + 8}+\frac{4}{x + 10}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
solution: The two different denominator factors give the common denominator \(\left(x + 8\right) \left(x + 10\right)\).
The new numerator is \(\left(8\right)\left(x + 10\right)+4\left(x + 8\right)\). Expand it and collect like terms.
The simplified result is \(\frac{12 x + 112}{\left(x + 8\right) \left(x + 10\right)}\).
The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -8,\quad x\ne -10\).

examples.title: Check for cancellation after combining
examples.question: Write \(\frac{x + 11}{x + 8}-\frac{15}{\left(x + 8\right) \left(x + 13\right)}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
solution: Use the denominator \(\left(x + 8\right) \left(x + 13\right)\). Multiply the first numerator by \(x + 13\).
The combined numerator \(x^{2} + 24 x + 128\) factorises as \(\left(x + 8\right) \left(x + 16\right)\). Cancel only the matching factor.
The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 16}{x + 13}\).
The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -8,\quad x\ne -13\).

examples.title: Subtract over two linear factors
examples.question: Write \(\frac{x + 20}{x + 10}-\frac{8}{x + 13}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
solution: The two different denominator factors give the common denominator \(\left(x + 10\right) \left(x + 13\right)\).
The new numerator is \(\left(x + 20\right)\left(x + 13\right)-8\left(x + 10\right)\). Expand it and collect like terms.
The simplified result is \(\frac{x^{2} + 25 x + 180}{\left(x + 10\right) \left(x + 13\right)}\).
The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -10,\quad x\ne -13\).

glossary.definition: A factor such as x + 2 that has degree one.
An expression that contains all factors required by each denominator.
One entire numerator over one entire denominator.

revision.body:
How do I combine two different denominator factors?

Look at the factors underneath the fraction bars. The new denominator needs to contain each factor from both old denominators.

For \(x+2\) and \(x-5\), use \((x+2)(x-5)\). Multiply each numerator by the factor missing from its denominator.

When can I reuse a shared factor?

Denominators can share a bracket. Use the largest power of each factor needed by either original denominator.

For \(4(x-3)\) and \(6(x-3)\), use \(12(x-3)\). The numbers 4 and 6 both divide 12, and one copy of the bracket is enough.

When can the combined fraction simplify further?

Collect the numerator over the common denominator, then try factorising it. A matching factor may cancel after this step.

Check the original denominator zeros before cancellation. They are still excluded even if the new formula shows fewer denominator factors.

Quick worked example

Write \(\frac{9}{x + 9}+\frac{3}{x + 10}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.

The two different denominator factors give the common denominator \(\left(x + 9\right) \left(x + 10\right)\).

The new numerator is \(\left(9\right)\left(x + 10\right)+3\left(x + 9\right)\). Expand it and collect like terms.

The simplified result is \(\frac{12 x + 117}{\left(x + 9\right) \left(x + 10\right)}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -9,\quad x\ne -10\).

• Keep whole numerators together.
  • Check whether the result reduces further.
  • Preserve every original restriction.

igcse-0580-af-factorise-and-restrict.description: Factorise polynomial numerators and denominators, cancel common factors and state the original restrictions.

blocks.html: First turn the whole numerator and denominator into products. A term within a sum is not automatically a factor of the sum.

figure.alt: Record the old restrictions. Factorise and cancel. Keep the same allowed inputs.
figure.caption: Cancellation changes the formula but preserves the original restrictions.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: If every term contains \(x\), take it out first. For instance, \(3x^2+21x=3x(x+7)\). Then look for the same factor below the bar.

blocks.title: Take out a common factor x
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(\frac{6 x^{2} + 42 x}{x^{2} + 11 x}\) fully.
blocks.hint: Look for a factor of x in every numerator term and every denominator term.
blocks.solution:
The numerator is \(6 x \left(x + 7\right)\) and the denominator is \(x \left(x + 11\right)\).

Cancel one common factor of \(x\). Preserve the two exclusions from the original denominator.

The simplified result is \(\frac{6 x + 42}{x + 11}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 0,\quad x\ne -11\).

retry.feedback: You cancelled x correctly. The leading coefficient still belongs in the numerator.
The factor x cancels. The rest of the denominator must remain.

blocks.html: If a term does not contain x, you cannot take out x from the whole expression. Test by multiplying your factors back out.

blocks.title: Factorise before cancelling a bracket
blocks.hint: Find factors of both whole polynomials first. Matching terms in a sum cannot cancel by themselves.
blocks.solution:
Factorise the numerator as \(\left(x - 9\right) \left(x + 13\right)\) and the denominator as \(\left(x - 9\right) \left(x + 15\right)\).

The common factor is \(x - 9\). Cancel it where it is non-zero.

The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 13}{x + 15}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 9,\quad x\ne -15\).

retry.feedback: This turns the fraction over. Keep the original numerator and denominator in order.
The remaining denominator comes from the factor that did not cancel.

sections.title: What if the numerator and denominator are quadratics?
sections.label: Match quadratic factors

blocks.html: Factorise each quadratic separately. A difference of two squares can give two linear factors without trial and error.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: Use \(A^2-B^2=(A-B)(A+B)\). Compare complete brackets from the top and bottom before cancelling one.

blocks.title: Use a difference of squares
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(\frac{x^{2} - 81}{x^{2} + 7 x - 144}\) fully.
blocks.hint: Find factors of both whole polynomials first. Matching terms in a sum cannot cancel by themselves.
blocks.solution:
Factorise the numerator as \(\left(x - 9\right) \left(x + 9\right)\) and the denominator as \(\left(x - 9\right) \left(x + 16\right)\).

The common factor is \(x - 9\). Cancel it where it is non-zero.

The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 9}{x + 16}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 9,\quad x\ne -16\).

retry.feedback: This turns the fraction over. Keep the original numerator and denominator in order.
The remaining denominator comes from the factor that did not cancel.

blocks.html: Brackets such as x + 7 and x − 7 have different zeros. Check the signs as well as the numbers.

blocks.title: Factorise before cancelling a bracket
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(\frac{x^{2} + 6 x - 16}{x^{2} + 8 x - 20}\) fully.
blocks.hint: Find factors of both whole polynomials first. Matching terms in a sum cannot cancel by themselves.
blocks.solution:
Factorise the numerator as \(\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 8\right)\) and the denominator as \(\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 10\right)\).

The common factor is \(x - 2\). Cancel it where it is non-zero.

The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 8}{x + 10}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 2,\quad x\ne -10\).

retry.feedback: This turns the fraction over. Keep the original numerator and denominator in order.
The remaining denominator comes from the factor that did not cancel.

sections.title: Why do some restrictions survive cancellation?
sections.label: Keep every exclusion

blocks.html: A zero in the original denominator makes the original fraction undefined. Simplification gives an equivalent value only where the original expression works.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: If a cancelled factor is \(x-9\), the original restriction \(x\ne 9\) remains even when the new formula has no such factor in its denominator.

blocks.title: Preserve the original domain after cancelling
blocks.prompt: A student rewrites \(\frac{x^{2} + 7 x - 18}{x^{2} + 9 x - 22}\) as \(\frac{x + 9}{x + 11}\). State the allowed real values of \(x\) for the original expression. Give the restrictions as inequalities or intervals.
blocks.hint: Find the zeros of the starting denominator. A cancelled zero is still excluded.
blocks.solution:
Factorise the original denominator. It is \(\left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 11\right)\), so it is zero at \(-11\) and \(2\).

Keep both exclusions after cancelling. The allowed values meet \(x\ne -11,\quad x\ne 2\).

retry.feedback: You found the remaining denominator zero. Also exclude the zero of the cancelled bracket.
You found the cancelled denominator zero. Also exclude the zero of the remaining bracket.

blocks.html: When asked for allowed inputs, check every factor of the original denominator. A simplified expression cannot restore an excluded value.

blocks.title: Use a difference of squares
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(\frac{x^{2} - 16}{x^{2} + 9 x - 52}\) fully.
blocks.hint: Find factors of both whole polynomials first. Matching terms in a sum cannot cancel by themselves.
blocks.solution:
Factorise the numerator as \(\left(x - 4\right) \left(x + 4\right)\) and the denominator as \(\left(x - 4\right) \left(x + 13\right)\).

The common factor is \(x - 4\). Cancel it where it is non-zero.

The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 4}{x + 13}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 4,\quad x\ne -13\).

retry.feedback: This turns the fraction over. Keep the original numerator and denominator in order.
The remaining denominator comes from the factor that did not cancel.

blocks.html: Keep the original restricted values on a separate line next to the simplified result.

examples.title: Take out a common factor x
examples.question: Simplify \(\frac{5 x^{2} + 30 x}{x^{2} + 10 x}\) fully.
solution: The numerator is \(5 x \left(x + 6\right)\) and the denominator is \(x \left(x + 10\right)\).
Cancel one common factor of \(x\). Preserve the two exclusions from the original denominator.
The simplified result is \(\frac{5 x + 30}{x + 10}\).
The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 0,\quad x\ne -10\).

examples.title: Factorise before cancelling a bracket
examples.question: Simplify \(\frac{x^{2} + 4 x - 96}{x^{2} + 6 x - 112}\) fully.
solution: Factorise the numerator as \(\left(x - 8\right) \left(x + 12\right)\) and the denominator as \(\left(x - 8\right) \left(x + 14\right)\).
The common factor is \(x - 8\). Cancel it where it is non-zero.
The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 12}{x + 14}\).
The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 8,\quad x\ne -14\).

examples.title: Use a difference of squares
examples.question: Simplify \(\frac{x^{2} - 64}{x^{2} + 7 x - 120}\) fully.
solution: Factorise the numerator as \(\left(x - 8\right) \left(x + 8\right)\) and the denominator as \(\left(x - 8\right) \left(x + 15\right)\).
The common factor is \(x - 8\). Cancel it where it is non-zero.
The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 8}{x + 15}\).
The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 8,\quad x\ne -15\).

examples.title: Factorise before cancelling a bracket
examples.question: Simplify \(\frac{x^{2} + 5 x - 150}{x^{2} + 7 x - 170}\) fully.
solution: Factorise the numerator as \(\left(x - 10\right) \left(x + 15\right)\) and the denominator as \(\left(x - 10\right) \left(x + 17\right)\).
The common factor is \(x - 10\). Cancel it where it is non-zero.
The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 15}{x + 17}\).
The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 10,\quad x\ne -17\).

examples.title: Preserve the original domain after cancelling
examples.question: A student rewrites \(\frac{x^{2} + 6 x - 160}{x^{2} + 8 x - 180}\) as \(\frac{x + 16}{x + 18}\). State the allowed real values of \(x\) for the original expression. Give the restrictions as inequalities or intervals.
solution: Factorise the original denominator. It is \(\left(x - 10\right) \left(x + 18\right)\), so it is zero at \(-18\) and \(10\).
Keep both exclusions after cancelling. The allowed values meet \(x\ne -18,\quad x\ne 10\).

examples.title: Use a difference of squares
examples.question: Simplify \(\frac{x^{2} - 9}{x^{2} + 9 x - 36}\) fully.
solution: Factorise the numerator as \(\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 3\right)\) and the denominator as \(\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 12\right)\).
The common factor is \(x - 3\). Cancel it where it is non-zero.
The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 3}{x + 12}\).
The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 3,\quad x\ne -12\).

extraPractice.title: Take out a common factor x
extraPractice.prompt: Simplify \(\frac{10 x^{2} + 20 x}{x^{2} + 7 x}\) fully.
extraPractice.hint: Look for a factor of x in every numerator term and every denominator term.
extraPractice.solution:
The numerator is \(10 x \left(x + 2\right)\) and the denominator is \(x \left(x + 7\right)\).

Cancel one common factor of \(x\). Preserve the two exclusions from the original denominator.

The simplified result is \(\frac{10 x + 20}{x + 7}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 0,\quad x\ne -7\).

retry.feedback: You cancelled x correctly. The leading coefficient still belongs in the numerator.
The factor x cancels. The rest of the denominator must remain.

extraPractice.title: Factorise before cancelling a bracket
extraPractice.prompt: Simplify \(\frac{x^{2} + 5 x - 24}{x^{2} + 7 x - 30}\) fully.
extraPractice.hint: Find factors of both whole polynomials first. Matching terms in a sum cannot cancel by themselves.
extraPractice.solution:
Factorise the numerator as \(\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 8\right)\) and the denominator as \(\left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 10\right)\).

The common factor is \(x - 3\). Cancel it where it is non-zero.

The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 8}{x + 10}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 3,\quad x\ne -10\).

retry.feedback: This turns the fraction over. Keep the original numerator and denominator in order.
The remaining denominator comes from the factor that did not cancel.

extraPractice.title: Preserve the original domain after cancelling
extraPractice.prompt: A student rewrites \(\frac{x^{2} + 7 x - 78}{x^{2} + 9 x - 90}\) as \(\frac{x + 13}{x + 15}\). State the allowed real values of \(x\) for the original expression. Give the restrictions as inequalities or intervals.
extraPractice.hint: Find the zeros of the starting denominator. A cancelled zero is still excluded.
extraPractice.solution:
Factorise the original denominator. It is \(\left(x - 6\right) \left(x + 15\right)\), so it is zero at \(-15\) and \(6\).

Keep both exclusions after cancelling. The allowed values meet \(x\ne -15,\quad x\ne 6\).

retry.feedback: You found the remaining denominator zero. Also exclude the zero of the cancelled bracket.
You found the cancelled denominator zero. Also exclude the zero of the remaining bracket.

glossary.definition: A factor of the entire numerator and the entire denominator.
The set of inputs for which the original expression has a valid value.

revision.body:
Which parts can I cancel?

First turn the whole numerator and denominator into products. A term within a sum is not automatically a factor of the sum.

If every term contains \(x\), take it out first. For instance, \(3x^2+21x=3x(x+7)\). Then look for the same factor below the bar.

What if the numerator and denominator are quadratics?

Factorise each quadratic separately. A difference of two squares can give two linear factors without trial and error.

Use \(A^2-B^2=(A-B)(A+B)\). Compare complete brackets from the top and bottom before cancelling one.

Why do some restrictions survive cancellation?

A zero in the original denominator makes the original fraction undefined. Simplification gives an equivalent value only where the original expression works.

If a cancelled factor is \(x-9\), the original restriction \(x e 9\) remains even when the new formula has no such factor in its denominator.

Quick worked example

Simplify \( rac{10 x^{2} + 100 x}{x^{2} + 11 x}\) fully.

The numerator is \(10 x \left(x + 10 ight)\) and the denominator is \(x \left(x + 11 ight)\).

Cancel one common factor of \(x\). Preserve the two exclusions from the original denominator.

The simplified result is \( rac{10 x + 100}{x + 11}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x e 0,\quad x e -11\).
revision.checks:
• Keep whole numerators together.
  • Check whether the result reduces further.
  • Preserve every original restriction.
revision.examTip: Keep the original restricted values on a separate line next to the simplified result.
